title: Clock & Calendar
subtitle: Angles between Hands, Mirror & Slow/Fast Clocks, Leap Years, Odd Days & Day of Week

TCS NQT.style: Angle between hands, mirror image, day of week after n days

Infosys.style: Odd days and century cycle questions, calendar repetition

Wipro.style: Leap year rules and basic odd-day counts

Accenture.style: Fast/slow clock gain-loss and coincidence times

readingSections.title: How a Clock Moves: Hand Speeds
readingSections.content: A clock face is a full circle of 360 degrees divided into 12 hours. Every problem about the clock is just about two hands moving at steady speeds and the angle between them. If you memorise the three speeds below, every other formula in this topic follows from them.

subsections.title: The Three Speeds to Memorise
subsections.content: Minute hand: 360 degrees in 60 minutes = 6 degrees per minute. Hour hand: 360 degrees in 12 hours = 30 degrees per hour = 0.5 degrees per minute. Relative speed of minute hand over hour hand = 6 - 0.5 = 5.5 degrees per minute.

subsections.title: 1 Hour-Marker = 30 Degrees
subsections.content: There are 12 markers around the circle, so each hour-marker is 360/12 = 30 degrees apart. At 3:00 the hands are 3 markers apart, so the angle is 3 x 30 = 90 degrees. Exact hour times never need the formula.

readingSections.title: The Angle Formula
readingSections.content: For ANY time, the angle between the hands is given by |30H - 5.5M|, where H is the hour and M is the minutes. This single formula solves every 'find the angle' question. If the result is greater than 180, subtract it from 360 to get the smaller angle.

subsections.title: Where the Formula Comes From
subsections.content: At H o'clock the hour hand has moved 30H degrees. In M extra minutes it adds 0.5M more, so its position is 30H + 0.5M. The minute hand is at 6M degrees. Difference = 30H + 0.5M - 6M = 30H - 5.5M. Take absolute value.

subsections.title: When to Take 360 - Angle
subsections.content: At times like 1:45 the formula gives 187.5 degrees, which is larger than 180. A clock can never show an angle bigger than 180, so the actual angle is 360 - 187.5 = 172.5 degrees.

readingSections.title: Coinciding & Opposite Hands
readingSections.content: The hands overlap 11 times in 12 hours, not 12. That is because the hour hand also moves. The minute hand needs 65 5/11 minutes to lap the hour hand. These follow questions are answered with the 12/11 trick.

subsections.title: The 12/11 Trick
subsections.content: To find when hands coincide between H and H+1: the minute hand starts 5H minute-spaces behind. Time to gain = 5H x (12/11) minutes. For 3 to 4: 15 x 12/11 = 180/11 = 16 4/11 min, so 3:16 4/11.

subsections.title: Opposite & Right-Angle Positions
subsections.content: Opposite hands are 30 minute-spaces apart; right-angle hands are 15 spaces apart. Adjust the starting gap to the target gap, then apply x 12/11. Example between 4-5 opposite: gap must go from 20 to 30 ahead, gain 20 + 30 = 50 spaces.

readingSections.title: Mirror Image of a Clock
readingSections.content: In a mirror, the clock's reflection swaps left and right. The reflected time is simply 11:60 - the given time. For example, the mirror image of 4:46 is 11:60 - 4:46 = 7:14. Answering is subtraction, no geometry needed.

subsections.title: The Formula 11:60 - Given Time
subsections.content: Treat the given time as minutes and hours, then subtract from 11 hours 60 minutes (which equals 12:00). 11:60 - 3:25 = 8:35. For 0:45 results, write the answer as 12:45.

subsections.title: Alternate Method: 12:00 - Time
subsections.content: Instead of 11:60, write 12:00 as 11 hr 60 min, then subtract normally. A mirror of 10:10 = 11:60 - 10:10 = 1:50. Double check by mental addition: 10:10 + 1:50 = 12:00, a full circle.

readingSections.title: Fast & Slow Clocks
readingSections.content: Some clocks are not accurate: they gain or lose a fixed amount each hour or each day. The question gives the gain rate and a set-right time, and asks what the clock will show at another correct time. This is just a proportional multiplication.

subsections.title: The One-Line Method
subsections.content: Gain (minutes) = rate per hour x hours elapsed. If a clock gains 5 min per hour and runs from 8 AM to noon (4 hours), it gains 4 x 5 = 20 minutes and shows 12:20. If it LOSES, subtract instead of add.

subsections.title: Finding the Rate
subsections.content: If a clock is set right at 8 AM and shows 12:16 at 12 noon, it gained 16 minutes in 4 hours, so the rate is 16/4 = 4 min per hour. Always divide the total drift by the elapsed hours.

readingSections.title: Leap Year Rules
readingSections.content: The Gregorian calendar has two types of years. An ordinary year has 365 days and its February has 28 days. A leap year has 366 days and February has 29 days. Cannot every 4th year be leap: century years (ending in 00) have a stricter test.

subsections.title: The Divisibility Rule
subsections.content: A year is leap if divisible by 4. EXCEPT: a century year (like 1900, 2100) is leap only if also divisible by 400. So 2000 is leap (divisible by 400) but 1900 and 2100 are ordinary years.

subsections.title: Counting Leap Years
subsections.content: In a 100-year span (a century) there are 24 leap years, not 25, because one century year is excluded (e.g., 1900 in 18xx-19xx). From 2001 to 2025, the leap years are 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024: six in total.

readingSections.title: Odd Days: The Counting Unit
readingSections.content: 502 week the counting tool for calendars is the odd day. Divide any number of days by 7; the remainder is the odd-day count. An ordinary year of 365 days has 365 - 364 = 1 odd day. A leap year of 366 days has 2 odd days.

subsections.title: The Anchor Table
subsections.content: 100 years = 5 odd days; 200 years = 3; 300 years = 1; 400 years = 0. Verify: 100 years has 76 ordinary (76 odd) and 24 leap (48 odd) = 124 = 17 weeks and 5 days.

subsections.title: Adding Odd Days for the Weekday
subsections.content: If 1 January is a Sunday, the same date 1 year later (ordinary year) has 1 odd day, so it is Monday. Adding 2 odd days moves the weekday forward by 2, adding 5 moves it forward by 5 (wrapping around the 7-day cycle).

readingSections.title: Day of the Week for Any Date
readingSections.content: To find the weekday of a given date, add (year last two digits) + (year quarter) + (month code) + (century code) + (day of month), divide by 7, and read the remainder using the day codes table.

subsections.title: The Codes to Memorise
subsections.content: Day codes: Sunday = 0, Monday = 1, Tuesday = 2, Wednesday = 3, Thursday = 4, Friday = 5, Saturday = 6. Month codes (ordinary): Jan 0, Feb 3, Mar 3, Apr 6, May 1, Jun 4, Jul 6, Aug 2, Sep 5, Oct 0, Nov 3, Dec 5. Century codes: 1600s = 6, 1700s = 4, 1800s = 2, 1900s = 0, 2000s = 6.

subsections.title: Worked Example: 25 May 2003
subsections.content: Year digits 03 = 3; 03/4 = 0 (quotient); month code May = 1; century code = 6; day = 25. Sum = 3 + 0 + 1 + 6 + 25 = 35. 35 / 7 = 5 weeks, remainder 0, code 0 = Sunday.

readingSections.title: When Does a Calendar Repeat?
readingSections.content: Two years have identical calendars (every date falls on the same weekday, and February matches) when the odd days between their January 1st dates total a multiple of 7, and both years are of the same leap/ordinary type.

subsections.title: The 6/11/28 Rule
subsections.content: An ordinary year repeats after 6 or 11 years (whichever first gives 0 odd days). A leap year repeats after 28 years. Check 2009+6 = 2015 has 2012 leap, giving 1x2 + 5 = 7 odd days, so 2015 repeats 2009.

subsections.title: Quick Exam Shortcut
subsections.content: For leap years always add 28. For ordinary years, try +6 first, and if the total is not a multiple of 7, use +11. Repeating calendars keep their type the same: an ordinary year's calendar only repeats onto an ordinary year.

readingSections.title: Days in Months Trick
readingSections.content: Fast counting of days between dates and month grouping is a giant time-saver in calendar MCQs. Knowing the exact day count of each month and the identical-start months lets you move between month-boundaries in seconds.

subsections.title: Days in Each Month (knuckle trick)
subsections.content: Memorise with knuckles: Jan 31, Feb 28/29, Mar 31, Apr 30, May 31, Jun 30, Jul 31, Aug 31, Sep 30, Oct 31, Nov 30, Dec 31. Month boundaries: the day added equals the number of days in the starting month (mod 7).

subsections.title: Months That Start Alike
subsections.content: In an ordinary year April and July start on the same weekday, and September and December too. In a leap year, January, April and July start alike; March and November also start alike. Use these to check day-of-week answers quickly.

formulas.title: Angle Between the Hands

formula.text: Angle between hour and minute hand at time H hours and M minutes.

formulas.whenToUse: Any question asking for the angle at a time that is not an exact hour.
explanation: Hour hand moves 0.5 degrees per minute.
Minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute.
Their difference is |30H - 5.5M|.
If the result is above 180, subtract it from 360 for the smaller angle.

example.prompt: Find the angle between the hands at 4:20.

formulas.memoryTip: 30 H minus 5.5 M, always take the positive value.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting to subtract the smaller angle from 360 when the formula gives more than 180.

formulas.title: Coinciding / Opposite / Right-Angle Times

formula.text: Time (minutes) after H o'clock for the hands to meet.

formulas.whenToUse: Between questions of the form 'between H and H+1, at what time do the hands coincide / are opposite / at right angles'.
explanation: At H o'clock the minute hand is 5H minute-spaces behind.
The minute hand gains 5.5 minute-spaces per minute on the hour hand.
Time to close the gap = gap x (60/55) = gap x (12/11).
For opposite: gap must become 30 spaces. For right angle: gap must become 15 spaces.

example.prompt: At what time between 3 and 4 will the hands coincide?

formulas.memoryTip: Multiply the gap by 12/11: it converts minute-spaces into real minutes.
formulas.commonMistake: For opposite hands, adding 30 spaces to the gap instead of reading the gap correctly when the minute hand starts behind.

formulas.title: Mirror Image of a Clock

formula.text: Subtract the given time from 11 hours 60 minutes.

formulas.whenToUse: Any mirror image of clock question in which a time is given on the dial.
explanation: A mirror reflects left and right across the vertical axis.
The mirror time always sums with the given time to 12 hours.
So reflected time = 12:00 - given time = 11:60 - given time.
For lt between 1 to 11 o'clock use 11:60 minus; for 12 write the answer as 12:xx.

example.prompt: Clock shows 4:46. What is its mirror image?
steps: Subtract minutes: 60 - 46 = 14, borrow 1 hour: 60 - 46 = 14 with hours 11 - 4 - 1 = 7.

formulas.commonMistake: Subtracting the minutes without borrowing the hour, giving something like 7:16.

formulas.title: Settings of a Fast / Slow Clock

formula.text: Add gain minutes, subtract loss minutes.

formulas.whenToUse: When the clock gains or loses a fixed amount per hour and you know its start time.
explanation: Compute the elapsed hours from the time it was set right.
Multiply the rate per hour (or per day) by the elapsed fraction.
A gaining clock shows MORE, a losing clock shows LESS.
To verify, answer should stay a plausible clock time.

example.prompt: A clock gains 5 min/hour, set right at 8:00. What shows at 12 noon?

formulas.memoryTip: Gain adds up, loss subtracts down.
formulas.commonMistake: Mixing up min per hour with min per day when computing the elapsed gain.

formulas.title: Leap Year Test

formula.text: Divisible by 4, but century years need to be divisible by 400.

formulas.whenToUse: Identifying leap year plus February 29 days, plus 366-day years.
explanation: A leap year is divisible by 4.
Century years like 1600, 2000 are leap only if divisible by 400.
So 1900 and 2100 are NOT leap years.
A leap year has 366 days, ordinary has 365.

steps: Must be divisible by 400, but 1900 isn't.
So 1900 is NOT a leap year.

formulas.memoryTip: Four, but hundred only if four hundred.
formulas.commonMistake: Marking every 4th year like 1900 as leap because it divides by 4.

formulas.title: Odd Days in Ordinary/Leap Year
formulas.whenToUse: Counting total odd days across a span of years to find weekdays.
explanation: 365 = 52 x 7 + 1, so 1 odd day per ordinary year.
366 = 52 x 7 + 2, so 2 odd days per leap year.
Odd days tell you how many weekdays to shift by.
Divide the total by 7 to track the leftover.

example.prompt: How many odd days in 4 years of which 1 is a leap?

formulas.commonMistake: Giving up the weekday shift without the mod 7 cleanup.

formulas.title: Odd Days of Centuries
formulas.whenToUse: Finding weekday of old dates, especially 1800s / 1900s calendar questions.
explanation: 100 years = 76 ordinary and 24 leap = 76 + 48 = 124 days.
124 mod 7 = 5 odd days.
400 years add 1 extras because the 400th is leap -> 21 mod 7 = 0.

example.prompt: How many odd days in 300 years?

formulas.commonMistake: Treating all centuries as 24 leap years; forgetting the one excluded (like 1900).

formulas.title: Day of the Week from a Date

formula.text: Adding the codes gives a number; modulo 7 is the weekday.

formulas.whenToUse: Given a month, date and year to find the weekday.
explanation: Add last two digits of the year.
Add floor(last two / 4) for leaps inside the year.
Add the month code and the century code.
Add the month date, divide by 7; remainder is the weekday code.
formulas.memoryTip: Year, Leap, Month, Century, Date - then modulo make ticket.
formulas.commonMistake: Mixing up the century code of 1900s (0) with 2000s (6).

formulas.title: Calendar Repetition

formula.text: Ordinary calendars repeat after 6 or 11 years, leap after 28 years.

formulas.whenToUse: Find the year with the identical calendar as a given year.
explanation: The gap must add 0 odd days total.
For ordinary year try +6 (1 leap in between) or +11 (3 leaps in between).
For leap year the only closed cycle is 28 years.
If the repeated calendar's year type changes, reject it.

example.prompt: Calendar of 2016 repeats in which year?

formulas.memoryTip: Leap spans twenty-eight; then everything old is new again.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding 28 to an ordinary calendar or 6 to a leap one.

formulas.title: Days in Each Month

formula.text: Month-day counts from January to December.

formulas.whenToUse: Moving between dates in consecutive months, or calendar-grouping months.
explanation: Thirty days hath Knuckle months: Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Aug, Oct, Dec have 31.
Feb has 28 or 29.
The remaining four (Apr, Jun, Sep, Nov) have 30.
Moving from 1st of a month to 1st of next shifts by month-length mod 7.

example.prompt: If 1 March is Tuesday, what is 1 April?

formulas.memoryTip: Jun asleep 30, 30 30 are the short ribs.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting February's leap year special case.

mcqs.q: How many degrees does the hour hand of a clock move in 1 hour?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: The hour hand covers a full circle of 360 degrees in 12 hours. Step 2: Degrees per hour = 360 ÷ 12 = 30 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: How many degrees does the minute hand move in 1 minute?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: The minute hand covers 360 degrees in 60 minutes. Step 2: Degrees per minute = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 degrees. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many degrees does the hour hand move in 1 minute?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: The hour hand moves 30 degrees in 60 minutes. Step 2: Degrees per minute = 30 ÷ 60 = 0.5 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: What is the relative speed of the minute hand with respect to the hour hand (in degrees per minute)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute, hour hand moves 0.5 degrees per minute. Step 2: Relative speed = 6 - 0.5 = 5.5 degrees per minute. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:00?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 3:00 the hour hand is at 3 and the minute hand is at 12. Step 2: On a clock face, 3 hour-markers separate them. Step 3: Each hour-marker is 30 degrees, so angle = 3 × 30 = 90 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 6:00?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 6:00 the hour hand is at 6 and the minute hand is at 12. Step 2: They are 6 hour-markers apart. Step 3: 6 × 30 = 180 degrees, a straight line. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 9:00?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 9:00 the hour hand is at 9 and the minute hand is at 12. Step 2: They are 3 hour-markers apart. Step 3: 3 × 30 = 90 degrees. The smaller angle is 90 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 12:30?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Use the formula Angle = |30H - 5.5M| where H is the hour and M is minutes. Step 2: At 12:30, H = 0 (12 is treated as 0) and M = 30. Step 3: |30 × 0 - 5.5 × 30| = |0 - 165| = 165 degrees. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: At 1:00, the angle between the hands of a clock is:
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 1:00 the hour hand is at 1 and the minute hand is at 12. Step 2: They are 1 hour-marker apart. Step 3: 1 × 30 = 30 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 2:30?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 2:30, H = 2 and M = 30: |30 × 2 - 5.5 × 30| = |60 - 165| = 105 degrees. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 4:30?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 4:30, H = 4 and M = 30: |120 - 165| = 45 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 5:30?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 5:30, H = 5 and M = 30: |150 - 165| = 15 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 7:30?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 7:30, H = 7 and M = 30: |210 - 165| = 45 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 8:30?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 8:30, H = 8 and M = 30: |240 - 165| = 75 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 10:30?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 10:30, H = 10 and M = 30: |300 - 165| = 135 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 11:30?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 11:30, H = 11 and M = 30: |330 - 165| = 165 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:30?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 3:30, H = 3 and M = 30: |90 - 165| = 75 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 6:30?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 6:30, H = 6 and M = 30: |180 - 165| = 15 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 9:30?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 9:30, H = 9 and M = 30: |270 - 165| = 105 degrees. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: In how many hours does the hour hand make one complete revolution (360 degrees)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: The hour hand moves 30 degrees per hour. Step 2: Time for 360 degrees = 360 ÷ 30 = 12 hours. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:15.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 3:15, H = 3 and M = 15: |90 - 82.5| = 7.5 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 4:20, H = 4 and M = 20: |120 - 110| = 10 degrees. Answer is option B.

mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 5:45, H = 5 and M = 45: |150 - 247.5| = 97.5 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 1:30.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 1:30, H = 1 and M = 30: |30 - 165| = 135 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 2:45.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 2:45, H = 2 and M = 45: |60 - 247.5| = 187.5 degrees. Step 3: Since this exceeds 180, the smaller angle = 360 - 187.5 = 172.5 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 6:45, H = 6 and M = 45: |180 - 247.5| = 67.5 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 8:20.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 8:20, H = 8 and M = 20: |240 - 110| = 130 degrees. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 10:10.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 10:10, H = 10 and M = 10: |300 - 55| = 245 degrees. Step 3: Since this exceeds 180, the smaller angle = 360 - 245 = 115 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 11:05.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 11:05, H = 11 and M = 5: |330 - 27.5| = 302.5 degrees. Step 3: Since this exceeds 180, the smaller angle = 360 - 302.5 = 57.5 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 12:15.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 12:15, H = 0 and M = 15: |0 - 82.5| = 82.5 degrees. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 9:15.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 9:15, H = 9 and M = 15: |270 - 82.5| = 187.5 degrees. Step 3: Since this exceeds 180, the smaller angle = 360 - 187.5 = 172.5 degrees. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 4:40.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 4:40, H = 4 and M = 40: |120 - 220| = 100 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 7:20.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 7:20, H = 7 and M = 20: |210 - 110| = 100 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 2:10.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 2:10, H = 2 and M = 10: |60 - 55| = 5 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 5:50.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 5:50, H = 5 and M = 50: |150 - 275| = 125 degrees. Answer is option B.

mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 3:45, H = 3 and M = 45: |90 - 247.5| = 157.5 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 1:05, H = 1 and M = 5: |30 - 27.5| = 2.5 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 6:10, H = 6 and M = 10: |180 - 55| = 125 degrees. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Find the angle between the hands of a clock at 12:40.
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Step 2: At 12:40, H = 0 and M = 40: |0 - 220| = 220 degrees. Step 3: Since this exceeds 180, the smaller angle = 360 - 220 = 140 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: At what time between 3 and 4 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 3:00 the minute hand is 15 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. Step 2: Time to gain 15 spaces = 15 × 12/11 = 180/11 = 16 4/11 minutes. Step 3: Coincidence time = 3:16 4/11. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 4:00 the minute hand is 20 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. Step 2: Time to gain 20 spaces = 20 × 12/11 = 240/11 = 21 9/11 minutes. Step 3: Coincidence time = 4:21 9/11. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: At what time between 5 and 6 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 5:00 the minute hand is 25 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. Step 2: Time to gain 25 spaces = 25 × 12/11 = 300/11 = 27 3/11 minutes. Step 3: Coincidence time = 5:27 3/11. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: At what time between 2 and 3 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 2:00 the minute hand is 10 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. Step 2: Time to gain 10 spaces = 10 × 12/11 = 120/11 = 10 10/11 minutes. Step 3: Coincidence time = 2:10 10/11. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: At what time between 1 and 2 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 1:00 the minute hand is 5 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. Step 2: Time to gain 5 spaces = 5 × 12/11 = 60/11 = 5 5/11 minutes. Step 3: Coincidence time = 1:05 5/11. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: At what time between 7 and 8 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 7:00 the minute hand is 35 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. Step 2: Time to gain 35 spaces = 35 × 12/11 = 420/11 = 38 2/11 minutes. Step 3: Coincidence time = 7:38 2/11. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: At what time between 8 and 9 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 8:00 the minute hand is 40 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. Step 2: Time to gain 40 spaces = 40 × 12/11 = 480/11 = 43 7/11 minutes. Step 3: Coincidence time = 8:43 7/11. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: At what time between 9 and 10 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 9:00 the minute hand is 45 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. Step 2: Time to gain 45 spaces = 45 × 12/11 = 540/11 = 49 1/11 minutes. Step 3: Coincidence time = 9:49 1/11. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: At what time between 10 and 11 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 10:00 the minute hand is 50 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. Step 2: Time to gain 50 spaces = 50 × 12/11 = 600/11 = 54 6/11 minutes. Step 3: Coincidence time = 10:54 6/11. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: At what time between 11 and 12 o'clock do the hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 11:00 the minute hand is 55 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. Step 2: Time to gain 55 spaces = 55 × 12/11 = 60 minutes = 1 hour. Step 3: 11:00 + 1 hour = 12:00, when both hands are at 12. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock are the hands of a clock exactly opposite?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Hands are opposite when the minute hand is 30 minute-spaces ahead of the hour hand. Step 2: At 4:00 the minute hand is 20 spaces behind the hour hand, so it must gain 20 + 30 = 50 spaces. Step 3: 50 × 12/11 = 600/11 = 54 6/11 minutes. Step 4: Time = 4:54 6/11. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: At what time between 5 and 6 o'clock are the hands of a clock exactly opposite?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Hands are opposite when the minute hand is 30 minute-spaces ahead of the hour hand. Step 2: At 5:00 the minute hand is 25 spaces behind the hour hand, so it must gain 25 + 30 = 55 spaces. Step 3: 55 × 12/11 = 60 minutes = 1 hour. Step 4: Time = 5:00 + 1 hour = 6:00. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: At what time between 7 and 8 o'clock are the hands of a clock exactly opposite?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Hands are opposite when the minute hand is 30 minute-spaces ahead of the hour hand. Step 2: At 7:00 the minute hand is 35 spaces behind the hour hand; to be opposite it must come 30 spaces behind, i.e., gain 5 spaces. Step 3: 5 × 12/11 = 60/11 = 5 5/11 minutes. Step 4: Time = 7:05 5/11. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: At what time between 8 and 9 o'clock are the hands of a clock exactly opposite?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 8:00 the minute hand is 40 spaces behind the hour hand; for opposite hands it must come 30 spaces behind, i.e., gain 10 spaces. Step 2: 10 × 12/11 = 120/11 = 10 10/11 minutes. Step 3: Time = 8:10 10/11. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock are the hands of a clock at right angles (first time)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Hands are at right angles when they are 15 minute-spaces apart. Step 2: At 4:00 the minute hand is 20 spaces behind the hour hand; it must come 15 spaces behind, i.e., gain 5 spaces. Step 3: 5 × 12/11 = 60/11 = 5 5/11 minutes. Step 4: Time = 4:05 5/11. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: At what time between 9 and 10 o'clock are the hands of a clock at right angles (first time)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 9:00 the minute hand is 45 spaces behind the hour hand; for a right angle it must come 15 spaces behind, i.e., gain 45 - 15 = 30 spaces. Step 2: 30 × 12/11 = 360/11 = 32 8/11 minutes. Step 3: Time = 9:32 8/11. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: At what time between 2 and 3 o'clock are the hands of a clock at right angles (first time)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 2:00 the minute hand is 10 spaces behind the hour hand; for a right angle it must come 15 spaces behind, i.e., gain 5 spaces. Step 2: 5 × 12/11 = 60/11 = 5 5/11 minutes. Step 3: Time = 2:05 5/11. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: How many times do the hands of a clock coincide in 12 hours?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: The hands coincide 11 times in 12 hours. Step 2: They coincide once every 65 5/11 minutes; 12 hours = 720 minutes = 720 ÷ (720/11) = 11 times (including 12:00 counted once). Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many times are the hands of a clock exactly opposite in 12 hours?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: The hands are exactly opposite 11 times in 12 hours. Step 2: Starting at 6:00, the hands become opposite once every 65 5/11 minutes, giving 11 occurrences in 12 hours. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many times do the hands of a clock form a right angle (90 degrees) in 12 hours?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: In every hour the hands form right angles twice, except between 3-4 and 9-10 where it happens only once each (the other occurrence falls at the exact hour boundary). Step 2: Total = 22 times in 12 hours. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 4:46. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 4:46 = 7:14. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 3:25. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 3:25 = 8:35. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 9:05. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 9:05 = 2:55. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 10:10. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 10:10 = 1:50. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 5:40. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 5:40 = 6:20. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 2:30. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 2:30 = 9:30. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 11:15. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 11:15 = 0:45, which is written as 12:45. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 7:52. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 7:52 = 4:08. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 1:01. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 1:01 = 10:59. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 8:40. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 8:40 = 3:20. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 6:30. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 6:30 = 5:30. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 12:30. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 12:30 = 11:30. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A clock gains 5 minutes per hour. It is set right at 8:00 AM. What time will it show at 12:00 noon?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Time elapsed from 8 AM to 12 noon = 4 hours. Step 2: Gain = 4 × 5 = 20 minutes. Step 3: Shown time = 12:00 + 20 min = 12:20. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A clock loses 4 minutes per hour. It is set right at 10:00 AM. What time will it show at 2:00 PM?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Time elapsed from 10 AM to 2 PM = 4 hours. Step 2: Loss = 4 × 4 = 16 minutes. Step 3: Shown time = 2:00 - 16 min = 1:44. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A clock is 10 minutes slow. It gains 5 minutes every hour. After how many hours will it show the correct time?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: The clock must recover a deficit of 10 minutes. Step 2: It gains 5 minutes per hour. Step 3: Time needed = 10 ÷ 5 = 2 hours. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A clock gains 2 minutes per hour. It is set right at 12:00 noon. What time will it show at 6:00 PM?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Time elapsed from 12 noon to 6 PM = 6 hours. Step 2: Gain = 6 × 2 = 12 minutes. Step 3: Shown time = 6:00 + 12 min = 6:12. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A clock loses 3 minutes per hour. It is set right at 9:00 AM. What time will it show at 1:00 PM?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Time elapsed from 9 AM to 1 PM = 4 hours. Step 2: Loss = 4 × 3 = 12 minutes. Step 3: Shown time = 1:00 - 12 min = 12:48. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A clock is set right at 8:00 AM and shows 12:16 at 12:00 noon. How many minutes does it gain per hour?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Time elapsed = 4 hours; gain shown = 16 minutes. Step 2: Gain per hour = 16 ÷ 4 = 4 minutes. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: A clock set right at 10:00 AM shows 2:12 at 2:00 PM. The clock is:
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Time elapsed = 4 hours; shown gain = 12 minutes. Step 2: Gain per hour = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 minutes. Step 3: Since it shows more than the correct time, it is fast by 3 min/hour. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A clock gains $\frac{5}{11}$ minutes every hour. How many minutes does it gain per day?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Gain per day = gain per hour × 24. Step 2: (5/11) × 24 = 120/11 = 10 10/11 minutes. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: A clock gains 10 minutes per day. It is set right at 12:00 noon. What time will it show at midnight?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: From noon to midnight is 12 hours = half a day. Step 2: Gain in 12 hours = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 minutes. Step 3: Shown time = 12:00 + 5 min = 12:05. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A clock loses 10 minutes per day. It is set right at 12:00 noon. What time will it show at midnight?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: From noon to midnight is 12 hours = half a day. Step 2: Loss in 12 hours = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 minutes. Step 3: Shown time = 12:00 - 5 min = 11:55. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 12:00 when the correct time is 11:50. The clock is:
mcqs.exp: Step 1: The clock shows 12:00 while the correct time is 11:50. Step 2: 12:00 is ahead of 11:50 by 10 minutes. Step 3: The clock is fast by 10 minutes. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: The hands of a clock coincide every 65 minutes instead of every $65\frac{5}{11}$ minutes. The clock is:
mcqs.exp: Step 1: A correct clock's hands coincide every 65 5/11 minutes. Step 2: This clock's hands coincide every 65 minutes, i.e., sooner than correct. Step 3: Hands meeting sooner means the clock runs fast. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a leap year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: A year is a leap year if divisible by 4, except century years which must be divisible by 400. Step 2: 2000 is divisible by 400, so it is a leap year. Step 3: 1900, 2100, 1800 are divisible by 100 but not by 400, so they are NOT leap years. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Is 1900 a leap year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 1900 is a century year, so it is a leap year only if divisible by 400. Step 2: 1900 ÷ 400 = 4.75, not an integer. Step 3: So 1900 is NOT a leap year. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a leap year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 1600 is divisible by 400, so it is a leap year. Step 2: 2004 and 2012 are divisible by 4 (non-century), so they are leap years. Step 3: 2200 is a century year not divisible by 400, so it is NOT a leap year. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: How many days are there in the year 2000?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 2000 is divisible by 400, so it is a leap year. Step 2: A leap year has 366 days. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many days are there in the year 1900?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 1900 is a century year not divisible by 400, so it is an ordinary year. Step 2: An ordinary year has 365 days. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: How many days does February have in the year 2000?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 2000 is a leap year (divisible by 400). Step 2: In a leap year February has 29 days. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many days does February have in the year 1900?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 1900 is not a leap year (century year not divisible by 400). Step 2: In an ordinary year February has 28 days. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in a leap year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: A leap year has 366 days. Step 2: 366 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks + 2 days. Step 3: So a leap year has 2 odd days. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in an ordinary year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: An ordinary year has 365 days. Step 2: 365 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks + 1 day. Step 3: So an ordinary year has 1 odd day. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: How many leap years are there from 2001 to 2025 (both included)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Leap years in the range are those divisible by 4: 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024. Step 2: That is 6 leap years (no century years in this range). Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: What is the first leap year after 1896?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: The next multiple of 4 after 1896 is 1900. Step 2: But 1900 is a century year not divisible by 400, so it is NOT a leap year. Step 3: The next candidate is 1904, divisible by 4, hence the first leap year after 1896. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: In a leap year, the month of February has 29 days. Which of these years is a leap year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Century years (1700, 1800, 2100) are leap only if divisible by 400; none of them is. Step 2: 2000 is divisible by 400. Step 3: Hence 2000 is the leap year. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 100 years?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 100 years = 76 ordinary years + 24 leap years. Step 2: Odd days = 76 × 1 + 24 × 2 = 76 + 48 = 124. Step 3: 124 ÷ 7 = 17 weeks + 5 days, so 5 odd days. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 200 years?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 100 years have 5 odd days. Step 2: 200 years = 2 × 5 = 10 odd days. Step 3: 10 ÷ 7 = 1 week + 3 days, so 3 odd days. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 300 years?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 100 years have 5 odd days, so 300 years = 3 × 5 = 15 odd days. Step 2: 15 ÷ 7 = 2 weeks + 1 day. Step 3: So 300 years have 1 odd day. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 400 years?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 400 years = 4 × 100 years, but the 400th year is a leap year, adding one extra day. Step 2: Odd days = 4 × 5 + 1 = 21 (the extra day comes from the leap year adjustment). Step 3: 21 ÷ 7 = 3 weeks + 0 days, so 400 years have 0 odd days. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 25 ordinary years?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Each ordinary year has 1 odd day. Step 2: 25 ordinary years = 25 odd days. Step 3: 25 ÷ 7 = 3 weeks + 4 days, so 4 odd days. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 10 years (2 leap years and 8 ordinary years)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Odd days from 8 ordinary years = 8 × 1 = 8. Step 2: Odd days from 2 leap years = 2 × 2 = 4. Step 3: Total = 8 + 4 = 12; 12 ÷ 7 = 1 week + 5 days, so 5 odd days. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 5 ordinary years?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Each ordinary year has 1 odd day. Step 2: 5 × 1 = 5 odd days. Step 3: 5 < 7, so the answer is 5. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 7 leap years?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Each leap year has 2 odd days. Step 2: 7 × 2 = 14 odd days. Step 3: 14 ÷ 7 = 2 weeks + 0 days, so 0 odd days. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 15 years (4 leap years and 11 ordinary years)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Odd days from 11 ordinary years = 11 × 1 = 11. Step 2: Odd days from 4 leap years = 4 × 2 = 8. Step 3: Total = 11 + 8 = 19; 19 ÷ 7 = 2 weeks + 5 days, so 5 odd days. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 365 days?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 365 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks + 1 day. Step 2: The leftover 1 day is the odd day. Step 3: So 365 days have 1 odd day. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 366 days?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 366 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks + 2 days. Step 2: The leftover 2 days are the odd days. Step 3: So 366 days have 2 odd days. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 500 days?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 500 ÷ 7 = 71 weeks + 3 days. Step 2: The leftover 3 days are the odd days. Step 3: So 500 days have 3 odd days. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 700 days?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 700 ÷ 7 = 100 weeks exactly. Step 2: There are no leftover days. Step 3: So 700 days have 0 odd days. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 14 years (3 leap years and 11 ordinary years)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Odd days from 11 ordinary years = 11 × 1 = 11. Step 2: Odd days from 3 leap years = 3 × 2 = 6. Step 3: Total = 11 + 6 = 17; 17 ÷ 7 = 2 weeks + 3 days, so 3 odd days. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: 124 days have been divided into weeks. How many odd days remain?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 124 ÷ 7 = 17 weeks + 5 days. Step 2: The leftover days are the odd days. Step 3: So 124 days leave 5 odd days. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 8 years (2 leap years and 6 ordinary years)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Odd days from 6 ordinary years = 6 × 1 = 6. Step 2: Odd days from 2 leap years = 2 × 2 = 4. Step 3: Total = 6 + 4 = 10; 10 ÷ 7 = 1 week + 3 days, so 3 odd days. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: What day of the week was 1 January 2000?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 1 January 2000 is a well-known anchor date. Step 2: It fell on Saturday. Step 3: Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: What day of the week was 15 August 1947 (India's Independence Day)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: This is a famous historical date. Step 2: 15 August 1947 fell on Friday. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: What day of the week was 26 January 1950 (India's Republic Day)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: This is a famous historical date. Step 2: 26 January 1950 fell on Thursday. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: What day of the week was 1 January 2001?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 2000 was a leap year, so 1 Jan 2000 to 1 Jan 2001 has 2 odd days. Step 2: 1 Jan 2000 was Saturday; Saturday + 2 = Monday. Step 3: So 1 Jan 2001 was Monday. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If 1 January 2024 is a Monday, what day will 1 January 2025 be?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 2024 is a leap year with 366 days = 2 odd days. Step 2: Monday + 2 days = Wednesday. Step 3: So 1 January 2025 will be Wednesday. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: If 1 January 2023 is a Sunday, what day was 1 January 2024?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 2023 is an ordinary year with 365 days = 1 odd day. Step 2: Sunday + 1 day = Monday. Step 3: So 1 January 2024 was Monday. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If 1 January 2025 is a Wednesday, what day will 1 January 2026 be?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 2025 is an ordinary year with 1 odd day. Step 2: Wednesday + 1 day = Thursday. Step 3: So 1 January 2026 will be Thursday. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: Today is Tuesday. What day will it be after 100 days?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 100 ÷ 7 = 14 weeks + 2 odd days. Step 2: Tuesday + 2 days = Thursday. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: Today is Monday. What day will it be after 50 days?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 50 ÷ 7 = 7 weeks + 1 odd day. Step 2: Monday + 1 day = Tuesday. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Today is Friday. What day will it be after 365 days?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day. Step 2: Friday + 1 day = Saturday. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: Today is Wednesday. What day will it be after 30 days?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 30 ÷ 7 = 4 weeks + 2 odd days. Step 2: Wednesday + 2 days = Friday. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: If the 10th of a month is Sunday, what day will the 25th of that month be?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Days between 10th and 25th = 25 - 10 = 15 days. Step 2: 15 ÷ 7 = 2 weeks + 1 odd day. Step 3: Sunday + 1 day = Monday. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If the 5th of a month is Wednesday, what day will the 26th of that month be?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Days between 5th and 26th = 26 - 5 = 21 days. Step 2: 21 ÷ 7 = 3 weeks + 0 odd days. Step 3: The same day, Wednesday. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: If 1 March is a Tuesday, what day will 1 April of the same year be?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: March has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 odd days. Step 2: Tuesday + 3 days = Friday. Step 3: So 1 April will be Friday. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: If 1 February is a Monday (ordinary year), what day will 1 March of the same year be?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: In an ordinary year February has 28 days = exactly 4 weeks + 0 odd days. Step 2: Monday + 0 = Monday. Step 3: So 1 March will be Monday. Answer is option D.

mcqs.q: What day of the week was 25 May 2003?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Use the date-to-day method: last two digits of year = 03, month code for May = 1, date = 25, quotient of 03/4 = 0, century code for 2000s = 6. Step 2: Sum = 3 + 1 + 25 + 0 + 6 = 35. Step 3: 35 ÷ 7 = 5 weeks + 0, and code 0 = Sunday. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: What day of the week was 20 March 1882?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: This date is the classic Zeller's congruence example. Step 2: Using Zeller's formula, the result maps to Monday. Step 3: So 20 March 1882 was Monday. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: If 1 January 1900 was a Monday, what day was 1 January 1901?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 1900 is an ordinary year (not divisible by 400) with 1 odd day. Step 2: Monday + 1 day = Tuesday. Step 3: So 1 January 1901 was Tuesday. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 2024 will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 2024 is a leap year. Step 2: A leap year calendar repeats after 28 years. Step 3: 2024 + 28 = 2052. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 2023 (an ordinary year) will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: An ordinary year calendar repeats after 6 or 11 years. Step 2: Check 2023 + 11 = 2034: years 2023-2033 have 3 leap years (2024, 2028, 2032), giving odd days 3 × 2 + 8 = 14 = 0 odd days. Step 3: So the calendar repeats in 2034. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 2016 (a leap year) will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: A leap year calendar repeats after 28 years. Step 2: 2016 + 28 = 2044. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 2009 (an ordinary year) will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: An ordinary year calendar repeats after 6 or 11 years. Step 2: Check 2009 + 6 = 2015: years 2009-2014 have 1 leap year (2012), giving odd days 1 × 2 + 5 = 7 = 0 odd days. Step 3: So the calendar repeats in 2015. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 1990 (an ordinary year) will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Check 1990 + 6 = 1996: years 1990-1995 have 1 leap year (1992), giving odd days 1 × 2 + 5 = 7, i.e. 0 mod 7. But 1996 is a leap year, so the calendar of an ordinary year (1990) cannot repeat in it. Step 2: Check 1990 + 11 = 2001: years 1990-2000 have 3 leap years (1992, 1996, 2000), giving odd days 3 × 2 + 8 = 14, i.e. 0 mod 7. Step 3: So the calendar repeats in 2001. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 2000 (a leap year) will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: A leap year calendar repeats after 28 years. Step 2: 2000 + 28 = 2028. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 2015 (an ordinary year) will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Check 2015 + 11 = 2026: years 2015-2025 have 3 leap years (2016, 2020, 2024), giving odd days 3 × 2 + 8 = 14 = 0 odd days. Step 2: 2015 + 6 = 2021 gives odd days 2 × 2 + 4 = 8, not 0. Step 3: So the calendar repeats in 2026. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 2011 (an ordinary year) will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Check 2011 + 11 = 2022: years 2011-2021 have 3 leap years (2012, 2016, 2020), giving odd days 3 × 2 + 8 = 14 = 0 odd days. Step 2: 2011 + 6 = 2017 gives odd days 2 × 2 + 4 = 8, not 0. Step 3: So the calendar repeats in 2022. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 2005 (an ordinary year) will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Check 2005 + 6 = 2011: years 2005-2010 have 1 leap year (2008), giving odd days 1 × 2 + 5 = 7 = 0 odd days. Step 2: So the calendar repeats in 2011. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 1996 (a leap year) will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: A leap year calendar repeats after 28 years. Step 2: 1996 + 28 = 2024. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 2018 (an ordinary year) will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Check 2018 + 11 = 2029: years 2018-2028 have 3 leap years (2020, 2024, 2028), giving odd days 3 × 2 + 8 = 14 = 0 odd days. Step 2: 2018 + 6 = 2024 is a leap year, so it cannot repeat a 2018 calendar. Step 3: So the calendar repeats in 2029. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: The calendar of 2012 (a leap year) will repeat in which year?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: A leap year calendar repeats after 28 years. Step 2: 2012 + 28 = 2040. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: At 12:00, the angle between the hands of a clock is:
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 12:00 both hands point at the 12. Step 2: They fully overlap, so the angle is 0 degrees. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: How many times in a day (24 hours) do the hands of a clock form a straight line (coincide or opposite)?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: In 12 hours the hands form a straight line 22 times: 11 coincidences and 11 opposite positions. Step 2: In 24 hours this doubles: 2 × 22 = 44. Step 3: So the hands form a straight line 44 times in a day. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: A clock shows 3:45. What time does its mirror image show?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Mirror time = 11:60 - given time. Step 2: 11:60 - 3:45 = 8:15. Answer is option A.

mcqs.q: What day of the week was 1 January 1900?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 1 January 1900 is a well-known anchor date in calendar problems. Step 2: It fell on Monday. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: At what time between 6 and 7 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: At 6:00 the minute hand is 30 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. Step 2: Time to gain 30 spaces = 30 × 12/11 = 360/11 = 32 8/11 minutes. Step 3: Coincidence time = 6:32 8/11. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: If 1 January 2000 was a Saturday, what day was 1 January 2001?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 2000 was a leap year with 2 odd days. Step 2: Saturday + 2 days = Monday. Step 3: So 1 January 2001 was Monday. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: How many times in a day (24 hours) do the hour and minute hands of a clock coincide?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: In 12 hours the hands coincide 11 times (once every 65 5/11 minutes, with 12:00 counted once). Step 2: In 24 hours this doubles: 2 x 11 = 22. Step 3: So the hands coincide 22 times in a day. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: If day before yesterday was Thursday, what day will it be 11 days from today?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: If day before yesterday was Thursday, today = Thursday + 2 = Saturday. Step 2: 11 days from today = Saturday + 11 = Saturday + 4 (11 mod 7) = Wednesday. Step 3: So it will be Wednesday. Answer is option C.

mcqs.q: How many odd days are there in 1200 years?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: 400 years have 0 odd days (400-year Gregorian cycle repeats exactly). Step 2: 1200 years = 3 x 400 = 3 x 0 odd days. Step 3: So 1200 years have 0 odd days. Answer is option B.

mcqs.q: If 6 September 2009 was a Sunday, what day was 3 November 2011?
mcqs.exp: Step 1: Days from 6 Sep 2009 to 3 Nov 2011: 116 days in 2009 (Sep 6 to Dec 31) + 365 in 2010 + 307 in 2011 (Jan 1 to Nov 3) = 788 days. Step 2: 788 mod 7 = 4 odd days. Step 3: Sunday + 4 = Thursday. Answer is option A.
